items.text: Credits
Updated the game credits to include localizers for the Tanuki Kabuki update.
Localization
Slightly enlarged the Brazilian Portuguese body text font.
Updated Brazilian Portuguese translations
Fixed delayed localization occurring when engaging with the Banzuke Boss selection in the Kabuki Theater after changing in a different language other than English.
Decreased wait times before being able to skip splash screens
Uzumaki Cave Design
Removed hittable statues next to Dodomeki in order to avoid a potential softlock in Uzumaki Cave
Slightly resized some platforms and removed a set of spikes in Uzumaki Cave’s Main Chamber.
Slightly changed geometry in Uzumaki Cave Herder Home, to make armapillo rolling a bit more stable.
Hello Steam community! 🦊
We’re back with another round of polish, fixes and improvements! This update focuses on smoothing out the early-game experience and expanding our language support to welcome more players to the fold.
We’ve been keeping a close eye on your playthroughs and bug reports in the
Many of the changes below are a direct result of your feedback on Steam and the Discord. Check out the full breakdown below:

This patch introduces Brazilian Portuguese localization and a series of "feel" improvements for Bo’s movement, including new input buffering tweaking for the grapple. We’ve also given the Uzumaki Cave area very slight tweaks.
Tudo bem! Brazilian Portuguese translations have been added for the entire game and all Steam achievements.
Added missing translations for the “Rearrange Furniture” prompt in the furniture shop within Bo’s Room.

Air Combat: Added a timer that automatically resets the air attack combo and cooldown after 0.6 seconds, making aerial encounters feel more in line with when a player expects to be able to attack again..
Grapple Buffer: Added a 0.12-second input buffer for the grapple ability. This should make "frame-perfect" grapples feel much more forgiving.
Tanuki Kabuki Balance: Slightly decreased Bo's staff attack handicap when the staff seal is active in the Kabuki boss rush.
Imperial Castle: All secret map icons inside the Imperial Castle are now automatically removed once the Sakura Shogun is defeated.

Developer Note: We heard your feedback! Players were distressed seeing icons they could no longer reach once the area closed off. This change ensures your map looks "completed" rather than "missed." Please be assured that there are NO critical collectibles in the castle.
Quest Balancing: Increased the timer for the top puzzle in the Armapillo Assemble Quest from 5 to 6.5 seconds.
Hitboxes: Decreased the hitbox size for battable cave rocks and projectiles to prevent accidental collisions.
Rearranged spike hazards in the Arena Puzzle area and Shimeji’s room.
Slightly adjusted ground geometry for the Armapillo Assembly Quest.
Added music and new enemy placements to Shimeji’s room.
Armakillo Boss: The helmet dropped by the Armakillo boss is now hittable once he's defeated. Go ahead, give it a whack!
Added a special particle effect when Armapillos are batted into walls.
Fixed an issue where players could aggro the bottom Sessho Seki in Shimeji’s room through a wall.
Quest Fixes: Fixed a rare softlock that occurred when talking to Moro after returning his children.
Fox Bride Escort Sequence: Fixed a rare softlock in the Fox Bride Escort Sequence triggered by a specific interaction between Fumie, Tsurubebi, and the grapple slice ability.
Cave Door: Fixed an issue where the locked door next to the Armakillo boss remained closed post-fight.
Save Data: Fixed the Kodama outside the Kabuki Theater not saving correctly.
Menus: Potentially fixed a rare issue where the pause menu/map became inaccessible after closing the Fast Travel menu.
The Fragile Egg Quest: The egg now breaks after 2 hits instead of 1.
Game Icon: Replaced the default game icon with a new higher-resolution version.
Various set dressing and lighting improvements across all regions.
[p align="start"]Hey Steam community,
[p align="start"]Just a small update this week that fixes some things that we caught from player feedback.
[p align="start"]Thanks again for playing! Please continue to give us feedback, comments, and suggestions, preferably through our Discord server linked below.
v1.2.5 Update
Player Controller
Fixed a bug that caused the input buffering for staff attacks to not properly buffer. The input buffer timer for all staff attacks is now 0.12s.
Bosses

Fixed occasional softlock in which the player would be blocked by an invisible wall when spawned at the end of the Hashihime wave chase after completing the wave chase and dying to the Hashihime boss fight without saving.
Fixed an occasional issue where Shogun would resume the much older final stages rather than begin the new chase sequence
Hello Steam community! 🦊

Today we dropped a new patch that fixes some minor things that were brought up in the first two weeks of testing the new Tanuki Kabuki Update. We're actively listening to all your feedback in our Discord about new features and ways we can improve the game. If you have any suggestions, please let us know in our Discord (join here: https://discord.gg/mvXDhcamxc) because we are the most active in there!

This patch focuses on resolving bugs and adding small new features to make the new content feel as smooth as possible. We added quality of life improvements and bug fixes primarily for the Kabuki Theater (Boss Rush) and the Doll Machine. You can now retry Boss Rush trials easily, and we've significantly improved the experience of collecting new dolls with new pull options and a reduced chance of duplicates. Several potential softlocks and visual issues have also been resolved across the game.
New Features and QoL Updates

Added an option in the Kabuki Theater boss rush to retry either the current boss fight if fighting a boss on their own, or to retry the Trial of the Tentaihana from the beginning, if the player died during a boss fight.
The “active” or “inactive” state of seals now persist between repeat boss fight attempts. However, the seals will reset to an “inactive” state if you restart the game/save file.
Bug Fixes
Fixed the Sakura Shogun in the Kabuki Theater boss rush fight occasionally travelling offscreen during the sword arc attack.

Fixed an edge case softlock occurring when talking to Okuni for the first time in the Kabuki Theater with the dialogue stingers disabled, only if they recently returned from the main menu or had little interaction with elements of the game that produce music stingers up until that point in their game session.

Fixed an occasional softlock occurring after fighting the base game Daitengu boss, in which engaging with an Omamori pickup and interacting with the Daitengu NPC at the same time will lock the player with no controls.
Fixed the playthrough timer occasionally being misaligned with the boss rush timer.

Potentially fixed an occasional issue of having the Trail of the Tantaihana victory logic and rewards trigger after dying and defeating a boss in the boss rush at the same time, most notably the Tengu Duo.
Slightly lowered the chance of getting doll duplicates after a certain amount of dolls are collected. We were already doing this but we lowered it even further in this update.
Added an option for “10 pulls” for the Doll Machine in the Kabuki Theater. This will be executed in 2 sets of 5 pulls rather than 1 set of 10 pulls.
Added a x2 fast forward option for the doll machine to increase doll reveal animation speed.
Fixed a minor texture clipping issue on Okuni's tail.
Fixed a material issue affecting the brightness of certain objects.
Reduced the emission of some particles in the Tengu Boss battles.
Applied a new hit animation to the sumo pagoda drums.
Fixed an issue where in some cases the camera would not follow the player properly when entering the wind tunnel in Megumi Mountain from the top entrance on the southeast side.
Fixed a potential softlock that may occur if a player repeats the tanuki race in Uzumaki Cave after building the kabuki theater but before entering the kabuki theater for the first time.
Fixed the player rapidly increasing in velocity in horizontal wind currents if wall jumping with no directional input in the same direction as the wind current.
Fixed the player grappling continuously when trying to grapple a moving small Gyochu as it is bursting from a larger Gyochu, before settling in a consistent patrol velocity.
Potentially fixed an occasional issue in which the player cannot access the Pause menu and map after engaging with the Fast Travel menu and cutscene.

Potentially fixed an issue some players have been experiencing with their primary rebindings being completely unbound when returning to the main menu screen and/or returning to the game after exiting.
Fixed unsupported and missing characters for the Japanese dyslexic font.
Fixed some minor typos in the English version.
Fixed a minor typo in the English description for the Moving In achievement.

notes.title: Patch Notes: Small Fixes & Community Feedback Update

items.text: Hey Steam community,
We hope everyone is enjoying the new Tanuki Kabuki update! We have been closely monitoring player reports and sincerely appreciate all the wonderful feedback and kind words we’ve received so far.
Based on that feedback, we're releasing a small update today that addresses a few rare issues that occurred during certain playthroughs and clears up some minor bugs in the new content.
Thanks again for playing! Please continue to give us feedback, comments, and suggestions, preferably through our Discord server linked below.
Bosses
Potentially resolved an issue where the daitengu boss would occasionally get stuck in Kabuki Theater boss rush fight. We will be keeping a close eye on this bug moving forward.
The “adding salt to the wound” achievement now properly updates when defeating The Sakura Shogun in the Kabuki Theater Boss Rush.
Other
Fixed an issue where Sakura City NPCs would occasionally not play the correct endgame dialogue if playing on the same save file in which the final boss was defeated on an older version of the game.
Fixed a visual issue with the speedrun and tanuki race timers overflowing improperly in the UI.
Fixed an issue where the Sakura Samurai in Sakura City would incorrectly appear in the post game if certain conditions were met.

The bridge to the Imperial Castle in Sakura City now disappears in the post game, to better visually indicate that the player can no longer enter the castle. Please note that there is no critical content locked in the castle once cleared.

releases.displayName: Major Free Content Update: The Tanuki Kabuki!

items.text: This major update introduces The Tanuki Kabuki Content Update, a free expansion that adds new post-game content, challenge modes, and collectible systems to Bo: Path of the Teal Lotus. Players can now engage in Boss Rush challenges, discover hidden Tanuki in the new Tanuki Tracker questline, unlock an extensive gacha-based Bestiary system and much more! The update also includes numerous base game improvements, quality-of-life changes, balance adjustments, and bug fixes aimed at enhancing gameplay flow, accessibility, and overall stability.

The Tanuki Kabuki Content Update has been added to the base game of Bo: Path of The Teal Lotus. To access the new content, players must reach the end credits of the base game and then load up the same save file again.
New Content Update Features
Boss Rush Mode
Solo Mode: Replay each boss encounter from the main game individually in a Kabuki-style stage setting.
Gauntlet Mode: Face a curated sequence of boss fights consecutively, testing endurance and mastery of each battle.
Seals: Optional handicaps can be enabled to increase difficulty in exchange for higher post-battle rewards.
Audience Reactions: Each encounter occurs in front of an audience whose reactions vary based on performance. Audience favor influences rewards.
Tanuki Tracker Quest

Added new questline located in Strange Garden. Players can locate and challenge hidden tanuki using Bo’s staff to reveal their true forms. After discovery, each tanuki can be raced in time-based platforming challenges. These quests unlock more features within the Kabuki Theater including:
Combat Rehearsal Room: Practice combat mechanics and experiment with various loadouts.
Tanuki Kabuki Band: Unlocks a jukebox for listening to soundtrack selections within the theater.
Bo’s Room Customization: Unlock and display various furniture and collectibles.
Gacha Machine and Bestiary
New gacha machine featuring 77 collectible dolls, spanning multiple rarity tiers.
Dolls represent characters and enemies from the game and can be viewed in a new Bestiary menu.
Dolls can be displayed within the Kabuki Theater on doll shelves that function as the game’s bestiary.
Bo’s Room Customization
A new player space within the Kabuki Theater.
Players can earn and place furniture, props, wallpapers, and decorative items by completing specific challenges within the Boss Rush Mode.
Theater Cutscene Viewer
A viewing room where you can rewatch the game’s animated cutscenes and credits.
Additional Features
New video setting, “Cinema Mode”, unlocks after reaching the end credits.
New achievements have been added for the content update.
Base Game Updates
New Features
Added attack dummy that displays total damage dealt by the player at the forge in Sakura City.
Added a player death counter to the inventory menu.
Bosses
Asahi
Asahi's lasers now deal 2 petal damage instead of forcing the player to reset to a checkpoint.
Sakura Shogun
A brand new final phase has been added.
An older phase has been removed.
Fixed the zoomed-out arena camera in the Shogun fight not changing if the player falls into a killzone during the illusion change animation.
Kabuto Yokozuna
The shide sawblades in the Yokozuna boss fight now give a jump reset when struck by Bo’s staff mid-air, not only for pogo attacks.
Gameplay
Extended invincibility frames for the player upon respawning (specifically during the respawn animation).
Removed several spike sets in the Thorn Maze of Midori Forest to improve flow.
Enemies
Fixed Kamaitachi (wind weasel enemies) in Megumi Mountain (near Ice Caverns entrance) not disabling for the remainder of the room after hitting spikes in the horizontal wind section.
Disabled collision damage for Mikoshi Nyudo’s (Skull Enemy in Midori Forest) body and added a distinct sound effect when hit by Bo’s staff.
UI/UX
Added a splash screen of the game’s key art on bootup.
Added Social Media buttons to the Main Menu linking to the official Bo Discord server and additional social channels.
Updated Main Menu layout/visuals and added icons for the base game and content update.
Bo’s Running icon on black loading screens has been centered.
Added gameplay tips below Bo’s icon on black loading screens.
Fixed the combo counter UI occasionally appearing in incorrect rotation. Updated the visuals.
Quality of Life Improvements
Added an additional input for dialogue scrolling on controller (Staff attack input by default).
Added an option in the Fragile Egg quest to respawn in the same room where the quest begins for quicker retries.
Added an additional checkpoint near the tengu spears in the eastern Ice Caverns.
Added a checkpoint to the Sencho Bridge wave chase section.
Adjusted spike placement and smoothed collider on Castle 3F right side (zigzag laser section). Added checkpoint before the section.
ToRi dialogue trigger in Midori Forest Burrows Entry now triggers only once per scene unless refreshed.
Bug Fixes
Fixed Jingu’s orb still applies damage to enemies if they re-enter their hitbox after initial damage.
Fixed player spawning off-map in Uzumaki Cave when entering the arena room from the right side and hitting a killzone.
Potentially fixed a rare Asahi boss intro bug causing an infinite loop in the intro animation.
Fixed post-processing sliders in video settings not functioning in certain Megumi Mountain rooms.
Fixed a rare softlock where mochi mallet platforms failed to load proper save states, blocking progress in Ice Caverns if fast travel was not unlocked.
Fixed rare bug where Bo loses control after pulling a Kodama if interrupted mid-animation.
Fixed game-breaking bug in Lower Kitsune Burrows where grappling could cause permanent ceiling lock.
Potentially fixed a rare camera issue on Imperial Castle Floor 1 when performing a Ken pogo skip over the right-side gap.
Fixed the Architect project list populating with unknown locked entries, making it look like there were more projects to unlock than there were.
Fixed an issue where the player could receive killzone damage during the transition from the Yokozuna Boss Room to the Megumi Mountain Summit after obtaining the Kabuto Wings.
Fixed a localization-related issue in the Japanese language version causing newly obtained items (such as Chomper Daruma and Kodama Charcoal) to remain visible due to UI fade-out lag.

Fixed an issue where the third-eye animation could persist after defeating Sakura Shogun when a third-eye Daruma was active at the time of the boss’s defeat. Fixed an issue where Kiyoshi’s dialogue could be triggered improperly after collecting all music sheets for “A Monk’s Melody” if the player interacted repeatedly during the fade-out transition.

Fixed a softlock caused by breaking a treasure chest and receiving an Omamori simultaneously while triggering Daitengu’s automatic dialogue, particularly when the Kitsune Kifuda item was present in the inventory.
Fixed an occasional softlock caused by talking to Kogi again after cleaning soot bunnies and before Kitane returned to the Armory.
Fixed the second eye for the exterior Daruma Shop not being filled in when the player fills in all the second eyes of their Daruma.
Other Updates
Updated sprite compression that has substantially lowered the overall hard disk size of the game.
Various visual improvements.
Various performance improvements
Added more Haikus to the Hall of Haiku’s scrolls.
Updated the end credits.

This small update addresses a number of bugs and includes minor adjustments to improve gameplay flow and player experience. We’ve fixed several softlock issues, adjusted specific gameplay sequences for smoother navigation, and polished some visuals. Thank you for your ongoing support and feedback!
Fixed an edge case where the player could receive killzone damage while transitioning from the Yokozuna Boss Room to the Megumi Mountain Summit after receiving the Kabuto Wings.

Fixed an issue where newly received items occasionally would not disappear in the Japanese language version, specifically for Chomper Daruma and Kodama Charcoal notifications. This was due to an unrelated issue causing lag during the fade-out of item gain notifications, particularly affecting UI blocks that are localized before appearing after the item received pop-up is deactivated.

Fixed the third eye animation persisting after Sakura Shogun is defeated when using a third eye Daruma at the exact time of the Shogun’s defeat. This was most noticeable when using a longer-lasting Daruma, like Third-eye Yuki.

Fixed a bug with Kiyoshi's dialogue where it could be improperly triggered when fading to black after collecting all music sheets for A Monk's Melody. This only occurred if the player spammed the interact button during the fade.

Fixed an edge case softlock where breaking a treasure chest and receiving an Omamori simultaneously could overlap with Daitengu's automatic dialogue, especially when Kitsune Kifuda was in the player's inventory.
Fixed an edge case in which the player could receive killzone damage while transitioning from the Yokozuna Boss Room to the Megumi Mountain Summit after receiving the Kabuto Wings.

Fixed the new item received occasionally not disappearing in the Japanese language, particularly for Chomper Daruma and Kodama Charcoal received notifications. This might have been due to a somewhat unrelated issue causing a serious lag while the item gained notifications were supposed to fade out, most notably UI blocks that are localized before appearing after the item received popup has been set to deactivate.

Fixed the third eye animation persisting after Sakura Shogun has been defeated when using a third eye Daruma right when Shogun is defeated. This is noticeable mostly when using a Daruma that lasts a while, like third-eye Yuki.
Slightly adjusted a ground collider at the Midori Forest - Kitsune Burrows Entrance to better match the visual representation of the terrain.

Modified geometry for the seed puzzle in Midori Forest Treetops to make batting puzzles less cumbersome. Removed a set of spikes on the left wall to prevent off-screen seed destruction and reduce player frustration. Added an additional seed sack above the first to reduce the need for off-screen batting.

Slowed down the speed of the Nurikabe Thwomp block on the bottom left of the third floor of the Imperial Castle. This provides a more forgiving window for jumping off onto the left wall while avoiding the moving lasers.
Reduced the rotation speed of the laser set on the left side of the first floor of the Imperial Castle. Removed the spikes on the left wall to give players more traversal options.

Increased the locked position time before firing for Asahi's Key Rifle Replicas on the third floor of the Imperial Castle, making the timing more lenient. Updated the reticle animation to better indicate when the laser will fire.
Removed a falling debris hazard from the first room of the Asahi Chase Sequence.
Improved set dressing in the Midori Forest Thorn Maze and Burrows Entry for better visual cohesion.

Fixed an issue where a 100% completion of the game was only being registered as 98% for some players. Players who have already fully completed the game and only received a 98% completion should automatically see the text updated to "100%" the next time you enter a save file that has 100% completion.

This update focuses on refining boss fights, fixing critical bugs, and improving overall gameplay. Key changes include improving hitboxes and better telegraphing for Sakura Shogun, Asahi, and Kiri Kiri Bozu, along with platforming and camera improvements to enhance immersion. Several bugs, including UI navigation issues and game completion tracking, have been fixed, and visual effects for attacks have been improved. These changes aim to provide a smoother, more balanced experience across the board.
Omamori Healing Fix: Fixed an issue where the Elegance and Progress Omamori healing effects would conflict with each other when both were equipped simultaneously.
Game Completion Percentage: Refactored the backend calculation of game completion percentage to improve accuracy.

Steam Sync: On save file load, game completion percentage on Steam is updated if the Steam percentage is lower than the local save file, to resolve cases where game completion failed to sync to Steam servers.
UI Navigation Fix: Potentially fixed an issue causing all UI elements in menus to become unselectable at random, especially for console and controller users.
Forge Scroll Camera: Fixed an issue where the camera for the Forge Scroll would not show the player when interacting with the scroll.
Boss Fight Changes:
Sakura Shogun:
Hitbox Adjustments: Increased the hitbox size of both the Sakura Shogun and the mask satellites to better reflect where damage can be dealt.
Shogun Clone Projectiles: Projectiles now increase in speed over time, starting with a slower velocity to prevent players from being insta-hit when too close to an attacking clone.
Shogun Projectiles Bat Icon: All Shogun projectiles now show a bat action icon when close enough to the player.

Sword Metronome Attack: Decreased the travel speed of the metronome attack and increased the sword arc travel time. The sword no longer clips into the ground during this attack, improving visibility for the player.

Laser Attack Changes: Lasers no longer reset the player’s position on hit but deal a pip of damage. The lasers start in a static rotation and then rotate clockwise after the telegraph. A new visual effect was added to indicate the laser direction during the telegraph.
Shogun Health Adjustment: Shogun’s health has been slightly decreased in phases 1 and 2 to make these phases pass more quickly on subsequent attempts.
Shogun Satellite Destruction: Grapple action can now destroy Shogun satellites completely without needing a secondary staff hit on vulnerable satellites.
Kiri Kiri Bozu:
Health increased from 30 to 33. Phase two now triggers when health reaches 15 (previously 10).
Slam Attack Telegraph: Kiri Bozu no longer tracks the player’s x-axis during the telegraph of the phase two slam attack.
Added additional visual effects to better indicate when the boss will begin dealing collision damage.
Asahi:
Asahi Hitbox: Increased Asahi’s hitbox size to better reflect the sprite.
Asahi Laser Lock on time: Asahi’s laser now locks on slightly sooner, giving players a bit more breathing room to dodge.

notes.title: Additional Gameplay and Level Design Adjustments

items.text: Improved Platforming Quality of Life Improvements:
Added a bump lantern before Kiri Kiri Bozu to aid new players during attempts.
Slightly modified the ground colliders leading up to Kiri Kiri Bozu to assist new players in navigating the platforming section.

Dodomeki Room Adjustment: Added an Armakillo and bump lantern to prevent a potential softlock in Uzumaki Cave for players attempting sequence breaks. A spike pit lantern has been repositioned for easier traversal.
Camera Adjustments:
Boss Fight Camera: Cameras in the Sakura Shogun fight now include parallax scrolling instead of a static camera.
Camera Hitches: Smoothed out jarring camera hitches in the following areas:
Lower Kitsune Burrows, near the arena.
First floor of Imperial Castle.
Other Changes:
Accessibility Option Change: Renamed the “Infinite Mana” accessibility option to “Infinite Tea” in English.
Samurai Stag Bug Trap: Added additional visual effects to indicate when the trap is aggroed in Uzumaki Cave.
Hi everyone!
Today we're pleased to release version 1.1.3 which focuses on NPC related issue as some general fixes and improvements!

Fixed a range of major NPC-related issues, stemming from a similar problem of pressing the interact input while a UI notification was active while talking to an NPC. It was essentially the same as the Daruma Shop game-breaker issue fixed in the previous patch but with other NPCs. The fixed NPCs include:
Daichi when updating the Vermillion Stranger Quest, and receiving a project available notification.
Asahi next to the Uzumaki Cave entrance, when receiving the Eye of the Beast quest.
Gyoji in Sakura City Tier 1, when receiving a project available notification
Kiyoshi in Midori Forest, when receiving A Monk’s Melody quest
Fumie after completing the escort in Midori Forest, when receiving A Fox’s Wedding quest.
Mitsaki when receiving the bunny blossom quest in Midori Forest.
Misaki when receiving and/or completing the infinite kettle quest in Megumi Mountain.
Mikami when receiving and/or completing her quest in Megumi Mountain.
Moro when completing the Moro's Monkey's quest in Megumi Mountain.
Gyoji when receiving and/or completing the Gumbai quest in Megumi Mountain.
Ko when receiving the Tengu Trial quest in Ice Caverns.
Kiki and Tombo when receiving and/or completing the Fragile Egg quest in Ice Caverns.
Kitane when receiving the Kitane's Crystals quest in Kitsune Burrows.
Kitane when receiving the Forge Upgrade project in Sakura City.
Daitengu when completing the Kitsune Kifuda quest in Ice Caverns.

Fixed edge case issue where the bamboo bat wall blocking the Uzumaki Cave entrance wouldn't disappear on room load after it's been destroyed. If the player has the Lotus Dash ability, the wall is now gone from the room no matter what.
A sprite sheet was left erroneously in the upper right part of Kitsune Burrows. This has been fixed.

Fixed occasionally getting frozen in place during the Ushi tea sequence when obtaining the Ice Picks ability. This occurred when spamming the “confirm” input while the Ice Picks UI notification was active in order to quickly advance dialogue.

Fixed the occasional hardlock when returning Iwao to Midori Forest. It occurred when you try to move immediately when exiting Kitsune Burrows with Iwao attached, then trying to hit Iwao out of the web before dialogue is triggered.
Fixed the reward for the second Sumo bout in Megumi Mountain not appearing occasionally.

Fixed the player's jump reset being canceled if one is already acquired while: opening the Daruma Wheel while airborne, opening the Pause or Tab menu while airborne, and involved in a cutscene while airborne.

There was an issue where players could be locked into the Sakura Shogun anteroom without unlocking fast travel first. This would cause them to be unable to return to earlier areas once they reached this room.: The player can now exit the room without fast travel via a scene change trigger in the bottom right that will place them at the front of the castle in Sakura City Tier 3. The player will then be forced to complete the fast travel quest in order to return to the Shogun boss fight and complete the game.
Fixed the Sumo beetle drums track appearing to play duplicate versions of itself simultaneously.
Various SFX tweaks and improvements.

Fixed a game breaking bug with all shops that sell Omamori Straps. If all items in a shop were bought before the Omamori Strap, and if the player proceeds to buy it, the player controller would freeze completely and not register the Omamori strap as bought.

Fixed coming back from a save file with an infinite loading screen.: Since it was the camera system looking for an invalid camera (which was saved improperly) in the room the player spawns in, it now checks for the default main camera in the room if a valid camera cannot be found on load.: There can be a case where the player spawned in a room where the infinite loading screen bug took place and the wrong camera in the room is active, since it'll only check for the main default camera of that room and there’s no way to check otherwise at the moment.

Fixed a variety of issues coming from the same Daruma Shop conversation bug. If the player pressed the interact input while the quest received or quest completed notification was active, the conversation would start playing with an invisible dialogue box.

This caused: a fixed camera that wouldn't change, all UI elements being deselected automatically in menus making it impossible to interact with the UI on a controller for the rest of the game session, and making dialogue with NPCs impossible for the rest of the game session.
Fixed Hitodama in the arena in Uzumaki Cave not being able to reach the player if the player is standing directly next to the bottom right gate.
Fixed Kabuto Wings visual effects still being active occasionally when the player is grounded and not gliding.
Bat Aiming

For controller analog stick inputs, the bat aiming direction now locks in the direction of your most recent input if no input has been made, rather than matching exactly your input and lack thereof. A deadzone was also added to avoid unwanted directional inputs.
Grapple
The grapple "field of view" has been narrowed slightly so grapple objects right above you within a certain range are not in the field of view when an up input has not been made.
Map
Dotted lines have been added to the map in certain places to more clearly show connections between visual gaps in the map.
Map Icons have been updated for better color coded clarity.
Minor update was applied to the Kitsune Burrows map to better indicate pathways forward.
Jorogumo
Jorogumo's "Bite Collider" has been animated to better reflect the area in which a player would expect to take damage.
Fixed an occasionally persistent hurtbox with Jorogumo's head. When certain animations were interrupted there would be a hurtbox that would occasionally persist when it wasn't supposed to.
Asahi
A few solid ground tiles are added in the last section of the Asahi chase to prevent players from wall rolling into spikes that are offscreen.
Hashihime
Fixed firewall tips deactivating prematurely in the Hashihime boss fight when their respective firewall travels offscreen.
Level Design
The ground that blocks players from going into Kitsune Burrows near the exit of Kitsura's boss room now disappears if the Fox Wedding quest has been completed.
Omamori

Providence Omamori effects have been tweaked slightly: 0.1 staff damage increase per 300 Fox Fire, with a maximum 1 staff damage increase. Providence Omamori stops increasing staff damage at 3000 Fox Fire.

Players were saying that the reward for the "Fragile Egg" quest felt underwhelming and we kind of agree, so we are buffing the "Elegance" Omamori by giving it a new passive effect while equipped. New passive: Bō will now heal at a rate of 1 petal per 3 seconds while hovering uninterrupted with the Kabuto Wings.
Visual effects have been added when gliding while Elegance Omamori is active.
Input icons for controllers were updated to more clearly show the directional input arrows.
Minor set dresing improvements were made in Uzumaki Cave, Midori Forest, and Megumi Mountain.
Tree of Blessing text now reads: "Pay 1 fox fire to read a blessing slip from the Tree of Blessings and refill your kettle?" in English only. Needs to be localized.
Improved Japanese, Chinese Simplified, and Chinese Traditional translations for Minori's dialogue near Kitsura's entrance in Midori Forest.

topNew: Map Icons have been updated for better color coded clarity.
Minor update was applied to the Kitsune Burrows map to better indicate pathways forward.

items.text: Hello Bōmmunity!
Thank you once again for all the feedback we have received so far. Despite some initial disruption post-launch we are beginning to hit our stride when it comes to updates.

For our second update, we've concentrated on enhancing game stability, refining gameplay balance, and improving the overall user experience. Key areas of focus include resolving bugs that affected progression and some interactions, ensuring a smoother and more reliable performance.

We've made adjustments to gameplay mechanics to provide a more balanced, intuitive, fair and less frustrating experience, including changes to recovery times after taking damage and enemy interactions. We’ve made changes to certain player controller elements such as the grapple ability, the shine dash ability and air attack combos. Visual and UI updates have been implemented to create a more immersive and cohesive experience. Additionally, we've enriched the game's content and lore with some new art assets and adjustments to some in-game areas.

These updates aim to deliver a more enjoyable, seamless, and engaging experience. If you left a negative review concerning the issues we've addressed in this patch, it would be greatly appreciated if you flipped the review to positive!
Much Love,
The Squid Shock Studios Team
Added new art assets in the Lower Kitsune Burrows for lore purposes.
Once a player builds the "Statue of the Hero" construction project in Sakura City, the stone inscription in front of it is now interactable and provides additional lore to the game.
Updated end credits to include additional Kickstarter backers' names.

The problem: Many players have perceived issues with the grapple ability. Sorting through the feedback we’ve identified the problem that players did not understand that they need to “hold” the direction of the grapple point and instead were “tapping” the direction resulting in unintended trajectories.

The fix: Rather than trying to enforce the “holding” of the direction, we made a change so that now you can just tap the direction. The grapple "field of view" that finds a grapple object, now keeps its most recent direction if a movement input is no longer made. For example, if you want to lock onto a grapple object that is above you, you can now point the movement input in the direction of that grapple object and let go of the movement input. Our hopes are that players, who were already engaging with the mechanic as intended, should feel no difference and players, who were having trouble previously, will now more intuitively grasp the nuances of the ability.
The problem: Players were perceiving a dropped “jump” input when dashing off of a ledge and trying to shine dash once in the air.

The fix: While this inability to jump was an intended consequence of not being “grounded” at the time of a jump input, we ultimately realized that it felt somewhat unintuitive to many players. So we have now made it so that if you are grounded when you initiate a dash you will always be able to shine dash even if you are not grounded when you input a “jump”. It is important to note that you will still not be able to shine dash with an air dash unless you have a stored jump reset. This certainly won’t allow for any cool sequence breaks………..right?

notes.title: Air Attack Combo Cooldown Reset QoL Improvement

items.text: The problem: Players were perceiving “air attack combo” cooldowns as dropped attack inputs.

The fix: This problem is something we are keeping an eye on and it is still somewhat unclear as to whether inputs are actually being dropped or if it's the cooldown that is causing a perception of dropped inputs. This is something that we will be paying attention to very closely moving forward.

In the meantime, we made a change where a dash will completely reset the cooldown on the horizontal air attack. Our hopes are that this change will allow players to gain a better intuition of when they should be able to attack in the air and reduce the perceived feeling of a dropped attack input.
Added an in game timer that is displayed on the top right of the screen. This is optional and the option to enable or disable the timer has been put in the Gameplay settings menu.
Removed the "Loading..." text from loading screens for a more immersive experience.
Made all Omamori slots in the Omamori menu selectable, even if an Omamori hasn't been obtained yet. This will smooth out the omamori navigation experience drastically.
Fixed an issue where Pyro-kun's description displayed the incorrect text in shops and in the Daruma Menu.
When fast travel is locked, its text in the map legend is switched to Vermillion Tongue, until the quest is completed to unlock fast travel.
Removed 2 erroneous map chunks from the map that were indicating that there were areas to explore on the third floor of the Imperial Castle that did not exist.

For stat achievements only, when the player loads their save file internal checks are made to see if the player has already met the conditions for the achievement, then triggers achievement completed if it hasn't been registered to Steam yet.

Increased Bo’s invincibility-frame duration after taking damage from 1.75s to 2.25s and from 2.25 seconds to 2.75 seconds if only 1 health pip is left. Our hopes are that this will provide players more time to recover and reposition safely.
Fixed the Sakura Shogun's hit material to give better visual feedback on when he is receiving damage during the boss fight.
Fixed a bug in the Megumi Mountain targets minigame that prevented it from restarting correctly from a saved file, blocking progression.
Fixed issues where NPC and quest values would occasionally reset between game sessions, potentially causing game-breaking bugs.
Fixed the Dragon NPC, Daichi, not triggering dialogue occasionally, which locked players out of unlocking the Library Floor 2 project.
Fixed an exploit that allowed players to skip the Jorogumo boss fight entirely.
Fixed the “game completion percentage” being inaccurately increased when defeating Sakura Shogun more than once on the same save file.

Made stat achievements more accurately reflect the player's inventory, reducing errors and making it easier to track progress. Players who have previously expressed stat achievements not activating should see these achievements active on their next initiation of a save file

The NPC “Minori'' now appears next to the entrance of Kitsura's boss room after the player dies once while fighting Kitsura. Minori will hint that players might want to upgrade their stats before retrying. The player is still able to attempt the optional boss at their leisure in spite of this. Please note that the non-English localization of this dialogue may be a bit rough before we get the official translations in.

Decreased Sakura Shogun's laser rotation speed in the phase 3 arena by 25% to give players more agency in Tsuki dashing through them.: Developer Note: We are still in the process of collecting feedback about this fight as it seems to be fairly controversial, especially with the pacing and variance in attacks. Our goal is not to make this fight easier, it is to make it more dynamic. We are keeping a close eye on feedback and will continue to improve it over time.
Fixed Jorogumo's head hurtbox not deactivating after her Flamethrower attacks if her Flamethrower animations have been interrupted.
Ice Caverns
Added 1 and removed 1 "tengu wall dash staff" in the Eastern Tengu Trials to achieve better flow in Bo's movement throughout the level.

A black shroud that previously covered a hidden checkpoint in the Eastern Column of the Tengu Trials has been removed. This shroud covered a very convenient checkpoint that a lot of players were just completely missing. Players who would go out of their way to discover this shrine checkpoint wouldn't actually need it as much as the players who completely miss it. So we have made its discovery more obvious.
Slowed down a rotating hazard in the Western Column in Ice Caverns in the first skull target section to make it feel fairer and allow for better player mobility.
Midori Forest
Repositioned some tsurubebi (blue flame rope) enemies in Midori Forest that were previously placed in a clunky way causing players to take awkward damage.

Certain elements of the seed puzzle before the bride escort have been added or rearranged to create better angles for batting the seed. The camera was also zoomed out to give a better field of view for elements that were previously off-screen in some cases.
Kitsune Burrows
Repositioned a grapple lantern and removed unnecessary spikes in the Bug Nest area in Kitsune Burrows to improve player flow.
Sencho Bridge

We changed one lantern set up in the Hashime wave chase sequence that we identified as awkward. An early set of 3 vertical orange bump lanterns was replaced with a single yellow vertical trolley lantern. Additionally, a small section of solid ground was added to the section immediately to the right of the aforementioned setup. This solid ground should provide a brief respite for certain players that had difficulty with the small window for a pogo, while also not taking away the opportunity to pull off higher-skilled tech for others. These changes were made to mitigate the frustration and difficulty in the first third of the chase while the last two thirds of the chase remained untouched.
Boats were somewhat increased in size in the first part of Sencho Bridge. This was done to give players more agency in maneuvering the boat while enemies were swarming them.
Applied a new animation to Sencho Bridge candles when they are hit.
Imperial Castle

Removed a destructible crate on the third floor of the Imperial Castle that hid a saving shrine. Players were often missing this shrine and then having to reset to their progress too far. In this particular instance it felt really bad to obscure its location from the player. Especially when many of the saving shrine locations are already obscured in the castle.

Increased the damage collider for Chomper's secondary action command to chomp, making it easier to hit. Players were having difficulty landing Chomper's secondary action command to chomp in its current position during Chomper's dash. We have increased the damage collider for Chomper's chomp so players can hit the chomp more reliably.

Fixed a memory leak with one of the controllers for SFX that could also have affected dialogue system interactions. This should increase performance throughout the game and greatly reduce game crashes where previously present.

Fixed a game breaking issue for certain autosave moments in the game where the game would be in an infinite loading screen and corrupt a player's save file when returning to that same save file from the main menu.
Fixed a minor memory leak regarding rebinding operations.
Dialogue for giving the Kitsune Kifuda to Daitengu is triggered automatically after beating Daitengu if the Kitsune Kifuda is currently in your inventory.
Globally increased the hitbox for all bump lanterns slightly to reduce platforming frustrations and enhance the players flow state.
Extended a scene change trigger in the Imperial Castle Entrance to prevent players from bypassing it by pogoing off a statue.
Fixed a minor memory leak regarding input rebinding operations
Hi folks!
Today we're pleased to offer up our first update to Bo since launch, it's been a hectic few weeks but we're pleased to be in a position where we can respond to feedback.

In this update, our aim was to tackle a few high priorities issues that were relatively easy to implement for a first patch. We wanted to push out this patch as soon as possible with the limited resources we have right now due to a lack of previous publisher support.

There are still many things that we are working on, including some strange bugs that seem to be edge cases, but we think that these initial changes alone will greatly reduce the frustrations a lot of players have been experiencing so far in their playthroughs.
We apologize we could not get to every bug that was reported in this update as some of them are very fresh and unreproducible on our end.
Thank for being patient with us, and thank you for your ongoing support.
Much love,
The Squid Shock Studios Team
The overwhelming negative criticism that we received from the game that seemed to sour the entire experience was the penultimate boss battle in the game, the Asahi Chase sequence.

Players were frustrated due to the lack of checkpoints during the fight. We totally hear you and agree with this criticism as designers. To all the people that trudged through that section, seriously kudos, your sacrifice and tolerance for challenge will not be forgotten.
Saving Shrines were added to the beginning of each room of the Asahi Chase Sequence in the Imperial Castle area.
We will be closely monitoring other sections of the game where issues arise.

There were a few things that we wanted to have for release and which a few of you have asked for. We're pleased we are able to add them now, but we do understand some features should have been in for launch.
The game now supports Steam Cloud saving for game save files and the settings file.
The names of each area now appear on the map once the player enters the main entrance of the area for the first time.

“Bunny Blossom” map icons have now been added to the map if you have encountered them in your playthrough. Keep in mind that these might need to refresh for some players depending on when you encountered them.

“Tree of Blessing” Map icons have now been added to the map if you have encountered them in your playthrough. Keep in mind that these might need to refresh for some players depending on when you encountered them.
Intuition Map Icons added for the 3 new hidden chests in the Imperial Castle.
The default zoom level for the map is now wider.
2 wider zoom levels have been added to the map.
Fragile Egg Quest

A Saving Shrine has been added to the right of the spawn point of the fragile egg in the Western Column of the Ice Caverns. This shrine was added to mitigate backtracking as much as possible when players crack the egg.
We will be keeping a close eye on this quest as we understand its causing player frustration.
Sumo Pagoda Tournament

A small number of players have reached this area without obtaining the intended grapple ability from Midori Forest first. Two pogo bounce pads have been added to each of the two stages in order to aid the player in reaching the center of the ring without the grapple ability.
Misc
Deactivated an unnecessary checkpoint in Kitsune Burrows that would cause a player to spawn in an unsafe location and begin an infinite damage loop after hitting thorn hazards.

We received feedback from players regarding the grinding for currency that is necessary to 100% the game. We made the following changes in order to scale Fox Fire/Kitsunebi rewards higher in the mid to late game, while keeping the earlier game relatively the same.

A small amount of grinding might still be necessary for players who tend to not farm enemies naturally, but it should be considerably minimized compared to the release version. No shop prices have changed.

Mainly boss rewards are changed with the largest increase given to Kitsura, a difficult optional early game boss that players should be rewarded handsomely for defeating early (100 fox fire for each of those pesky tails).
Hashihime Boss fox fire reward increased from 100 to 200
Kabuto Yokozuna Boss fox fire reward increased from 250 to 300
Tengu Trio Boss fox fire reward increased from 333 to 700
Jorogumo Boss fox fire reward increased from 300 to 700
Gashadokuro Boss fox fire reward increased from 500 to 800
Asahi Boss fox fire reward increased from 900 to 1000
Enemy Arena fox fire rewards increased from 100 to 150 per room.
3 Chests containing 100 fox fire each are now hidden in the Imperial Castle.
The fox fire reward for completing the sumo target mini game in Sakura City increased from 50 to 300.
Kitsura Boss fox fire reward increased from 300 to 900
The slam hurtbox for the Kiri Kiri Bozu was reduced in size to better reflect the visual representation of the associated particle effect.

The vertical chochin are playable from the start and no longer on fire at the start of the boss fight. Upon reviewing feedback, it’s apparent this only presents a frustrating inconvenience rather than an interesting challenge in the fight.

Candle health is nerfed across each phase: Phase 1 candles HP decreased from 15 to 13 for a total of 26 HP: Phase 2 Candles HP decreased from 15 to 13 for a total of 26 HP: Phase 3 Candle HP decreased from 25 to 22 for a total of 22 total HP

Dev Note: A problem that we saw throughout the first week is that players did not realize that they could hit Hashihime’s candles for staff damage and instead were waiting for the water orb battable object phase in order to deal damage.

This made the fight seem incredibly long with a lot of waiting. We thought that training players to hit candles throughout the entire level would be enough to enforce this mechanic but we were wrong. We are currently thinking of ways to make this clearer in a future update.

The fireballs that eject from Kitsura’s tails are now red instead of blue. This change was made in order to provide more contrast from the background as well as to differentiate them from Bo's character color. Furthermore, changing the color also further clarifies that the fireballs are not battable objects.

Dev Note: Many players have noticed the intense difficulty spike for Kitsura. This difficulty spike was intentional as Kitsura is an optional boss in the game. Despite this we were surprised at how many players threw themselves at her in a masochistic manner and were saddened when they could not pet her after the battle. In a future update we hope to further clarify naturally that it may be a good idea for the player to return to the boss once they have become stronger.

A save shrine has been added to the second and third room of the Asahi boss fight. This is to reduce the amount of frustration caused by starting from the very beginning of this boss fight when dying in room two and room three. This also gives the player an option to heal completely before engaging in the boss battle after reaching another room in the fight.
Lanterns were added in the background of the Ice Caverns illusion phase with the intention of having greater clarity and contrast between the background and the player character.

Dev Note: We have more changes coming for this boss battle to better pace some of the phases as well as add additional ways to reduce player frustration. Specifically we want to give more options for the player to ascend and deal damage to the shogun when out of reach. These design changes however still need to be tested further and were not within the scope of this patch milestone.

Fixed an issue where the “Exorciser” (Kiri Kiri Bozu Boss defeated) and “Beast Tamer” (Particularly Unmanageable Armakillo Boss defeated) achievements did not trigger if a player was playing from a Next Fest demo save file.

The “Prosperous” achievement conditions have changed from “having 8000 fox fire currently in your inventory” to “having overall accumulated 8000 Fox Fire over time”. This will not affect players who already have the achievement, but for everyone else the achievement will start from 0 fox fire on Steam, since it is now a stat-based achievement with no previous record of total fox fire on Steam. We apologize for the inconvenience.
Fixed an issue where the “Particularly Unmanageable Armakillo” achievement would trigger at a 34 hit combo instead of the intended 33 hit combo
